correctness.rationale: The two possible length-two paths for each of the two cross-layer nonadjacent pairs give two Boolean conditions. Their complete truth-table reduction yields one forbidden ordered layer-edge assignment when rung colours agree, and equality of layer-edge colours when rung colours differ. Each unordered index pair controls exactly two distinct clique edges, so the conditional product counts every colouring exactly once. The minimum-degree formula follows by extracting lowest powers of each factor, with the only equality cases \(t\in\{1,2\}\). Colour exchange proves reciprocity; the binomial bound proves the total-count asymptotic. Direct graph-path enumeration checks all 16, 512 and 65,536 possible colourings for \(n\in\{2,3,4\}\) and 25,000 reproducible samples for each \(5\le n\le8\). Finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete coefficient-wise classification of every successful red/blue length-two rainbow connection on a natural Dirac graph family is a substantive strengthening of a two-colour existence assertion. The local pair-factorization reveals a separability not implied by general connectivity bounds. The result also solves a natural minimum-recolouring resource problem (\(n-1\) edges), classifies all \(n^2\) optimizers, and gives exact total counts and a sharp leading asymptotic for random colourings.
